class.name: InputBindings
class.brief_description: The player's own controls: bindings over the Input Map, saved for each player, with button prompts for whatever controller they're using.
class.description: The game's defaults are its Input Map (Project Settings > Input Map), and optionally a defaults file ([code]input_devices/bindings/defaults[/code], JSON) that can calibrate axes and add [i]contexts[/i]: sets of bindings that only apply while the game says (driving a manual, say). Each player's changes are saved in the user folder and loaded over the defaults; actions the game adds later get their defaults, and actions it drops are forgotten. A binding is a [Dictionary], saved as readable JSON: [codeblock] {"key": "W"} # a key, by where it is (Godot's name for it) {"mouse": "left"} # left, right, middle, wheel_up, wheel_down, back or forward {"device": "gamepad", "button": "a"} # a joypad button, by name or number {"device": "gamepad", "axis": "left_x", "from": 0.0, "to": -1.0, "deadzone": 0.1, "curve": 1.5} {"device": "Logitech G923", "hat": "up"} # a steering wheel's hat [/codeblock] [code]"device"[/code] is a joypad's name (with its [code]"guid"[/code] where known), so a binding follows its controller between sessions and ports, or [code]"gamepad"[/code] for any controller, never a steering wheel (some read as gamepads, their pedals as triggers). Buttons are named as Godot names them, by position: [code]"a"[/code] is the bottom face button whatever it says on it. An axis maps raw values from [code]"from"[/code] to [code]"to"[/code] (which covers its range and which way it goes), ignores the first [code]"deadzone"[/code] of its travel, and with a [code]"curve"[/code] above 1 is progressive. Player 1's bindings are put into the Input Map, so [method Input.is_action_pressed] and the rest work as usual. Every player's are read with [method get_value], [method is_pressed] and the like. Player 1 has the keyboard, the mouse and every controller nobody else has; give a local player their own with [method set_player_devices], and their own saved bindings with [method set_player_profile]. Presses the game makes itself, with [method Input.action_press] or an [InputEventAction], count for player 1. Each binding has a prompt: an image for the controller the player is using ([method get_prompt], or an [InputPrompt] node), or words ([method describe]). Purr's images are Kenney's Input Prompts, in a crisp vector style or a 16 by 16 pixel one ([code]input_devices/prompts/style[/code]); a game can use its own with an [InputPromptSet]. Steering wheels Purr knows name their own buttons ("Right paddle", "Gear 3") and show icons where a button wears one. Godot's own menu movement ([code]ui_up[/code] and the rest) is kept to controllers: a steering wheel no longer moves the highlight round the menus with its pedals.

method.name: bind
method.description: Adds a binding to an action, for a player, and saves it. An input already bound to the action isn't added twice.

method.name: cancel_capture
method.description: Stops a [method capture] under way; it completes with [code]error[/code] [code]"cancelled"[/code].

method.name: capture
method.description: Waits for the next key, mouse button, joypad button or axis movement on the player's devices, to bind. Await it: the result has [code]ok[/code] and the [code]binding[/code]. An axis counts once it moves well away from where it rested, and comes back calibrated from rest to the far end. Escape cancels ([code]error[/code] [code]"cancelled"[/code]).

method.name: describe
method.description: The name of what the player presses for an action now, on the controller they're using: [code]"Space"[/code], [code]"Right Shoulder"[/code], [code]"Gear 3"[/code]. Empty if it isn't bound.

method.name: describe_binding
method.description: A binding in words. Keys are named as the player's keyboard layout prints them, and steering wheels Purr knows name their own buttons.

method.name: export_bindings
method.description: A player's whole set of bindings, as they're saved: [code]{"bindings": {...}, "contexts": {...}}[/code]. For presets the player can pick, or sharing a set between players.

method.name: get_actions
method.description: The actions this manages: the Input Map's own (not Godot's [code]ui_*[/code]) and the defaults file's.

method.name: get_actions_using
method.description: The actions that a binding's input also works, for a player: for warning that an input is already in use.

method.name: get_active_bindings
method.description: An action's bindings that apply now for a player: its own and those of the active contexts.

method.name: get_axis
method.description: [method get_value] of [param positive_action] less that of [param negative_action], for a player.

method.name: get_binding_devices
method.description: The connected joypads a binding means, for a player.

method.name: get_binding_events
method.description: The input events a binding becomes on a player's devices.

method.name: get_binding_prompt
method.description: A binding's prompt image, as it shows on the controller it's on (else the one the player is using), [param size] pixels high in the standard style (0: [code]input_devices/prompts/size[/code]). Null where there's no image: show [method describe_binding] instead.

method.name: get_binding_value
method.description: How far a binding is pressed now, for a player, from 0 to 1.

method.name: get_bindings
method.description: An action's bindings, for a player (their own, or the game's defaults): those that always apply, or a [param context]'s.

method.name: get_device_family
method.description: What kind of controller a device is ([constant KEYBOARD] for the keyboard and mouse).

method.name: get_device_name
method.description: A device's name, for the player to recognise: [code]"Keyboard and mouse"[/code], a wheel's model, or the name the controller gives.

method.name: get_device_player
method.description: The local player a device belongs to: player 1 (0) unless [method set_player_devices] gave it to another, or -1 if nobody has it (once player 1 has devices of their own).

method.name: get_events
method.description: The input events of an action's bindings on a player's devices: for adding them to other actions (a game's menu controls to Godot's [code]ui_*[/code]).

method.name: get_player_devices
method.description: The devices a player has now: [constant KEYBOARD] and joypad numbers.

method.name: get_player_family
method.description: What kind of controller the player used last.

method.name: get_player_last_device
method.description: The device the player used last.

method.name: get_player_profile
method.description: The name a player's bindings are saved under.

method.name: get_prompt
method.description: An action's prompt image for a player now, on the controller they're using (see [method get_binding_prompt]).

method.name: get_prompt_binding
method.description: The binding a player would use for an action now: on the keyboard if that's what they used last, else on their controller.

method.name: get_value
method.description: How far an action is pressed for a player, from 0 to 1: the strongest of its bindings on their devices, axes calibrated.

method.name: get_vector
method.description: A direction from four actions, for a player, no longer than 1.

method.name: has_axis
method.description: Whether an action is bound to an axis of a joypad the player has (a handbrake on a real lever, held rather than switched).

method.name: import_bindings
method.description: Sets a player's whole set of bindings at once, as [method export_bindings] gives them (and the defaults file has them), and saves. Actions it leaves out keep the game's defaults.

method.name: is_axis_heard
method.description: Whether a joypad's axis has reported since it was plugged in. Until then Godot reads it as 0, which isn't where it rests (a pedal rests at one end): [method get_value] reads an axis it hasn't heard as at rest.

method.name: is_capturing
method.description: Whether a [method capture] is under way.

method.name: is_context_active
method.description: Whether a context's bindings apply now.

method.name: is_customised
method.description: Whether a player has changed their bindings from the game's defaults.

method.name: is_digital
method.description: Whether an action's strongest input now is a key or button, which jumps straight to full, rather than an axis.

method.name: is_just_pressed
method.description: Whether an action was pressed for a player this frame, or this physics tick when asked from [method Node._physics_process], as [method Input.is_action_just_pressed] does.

method.name: is_just_released
method.description: Whether an action was let go for a player this frame, or this physics tick when asked from [method Node._physics_process].

method.name: is_pressed
method.description: Whether an action is pressed for a player (an axis past half way).

method.name: is_steering_wheel
method.description: Whether a joypad is a steering wheel: one Purr knows by its USB IDs, or one calling itself a wheel.

method.name: reset
method.description: Puts a player's bindings back to the game's defaults, deleting what they saved.

method.name: set_bindings
method.description: Sets an action's bindings for a player (those that always apply, or a [param context]'s), and saves them.

method.name: set_context_active
method.description: Turns a context's bindings on or off (the contexts in the defaults file).

method.name: set_player_devices
method.description: Gives a player these devices ([constant KEYBOARD] and joypad numbers), taking them from anyone who had them. Player 1 has whatever nobody else has until they're given devices of their own; then a controller nobody has belongs to nobody, so it can ask to join without moving player 1. An empty list gives a player back what they have by default.

method.name: set_player_profile
method.description: Sets the name a player's bindings are saved under, so each of a game's players or profiles keeps their own. Players start with [code]"default"[/code], shared.

method.name: show_prompts_in
method.description: Shows [param text] in a [RichTextLabel] with each [code]{action}[/code] as its prompt for the player (or in words where it has no image), as tall as the label's text or [param size]. Show it again when [signal player_family_changed] or [signal bindings_changed] fires.

method.name: unbind
method.description: Removes a binding from an action, for a player, and saves it.

members.member: Where players' bindings are saved, one file for each profile ([method set_player_profile]): [code]user://input_bindings[/code] by default. A game that keeps its saves somewhere of its own (a folder its tests or a development copy redirect) can put the controls with them.

signal.name: bindings_changed
signal.description: A player's bindings changed: they rebound something, reset, or a context turned on or off.

signal.name: devices_changed
signal.description: A controller was plugged in or out, or devices were given to another player.

signal.name: player_family_changed
signal.description: A player picked up another kind of controller: time for other prompts.

constants.constant: The keyboard and mouse, where a device number is asked for.
A PlayStation 4 controller (or an older one).
A Nintendo controller: its bottom button says B and its right one A, and prompts show what's printed.
Any other controller, shown with Xbox prompts (SDL reads it in that layout).
